summary: Jeff Schomay presents his project building a game with entirely AI-generated content. The game is a simple forest exploration experience where players move from scene to scene, with encounters affecting Vigor and Courage stats, aiming to find home before courage depletes. Originally containing 16 fixed scenes in a 4x4 grid, Schomay expanded the concept to generate fresh scenes on demand, creating infinite unique playthroughs. For text generation, he began with OpenAI's completion endpoint using detailed, lengthy prompts that produced valid JSON scene definitions. To improve reliability and reduce token usage, he fine-tuned a model on 50 examples with simplified prompts, embedding the JSON format knowledge into the training data. This cost approximately $1-2 total and produced perfectly formatted output with fewer tokens. For images, he used Leonardo, which offers custom image model creation for stylistic consistency. The challenge was training data that balanced consistency (perspective, scale, forest setting, tone) with variety (people, animals, buildings, empty scenes). He trained multiple models with different parameters before finding one that worked, producing images with cohesive style but unique content. The complete pipeline runs through a simple asset server: request scene from OpenAI, validate JSON, send description to Leonardo for image generation, then assemble and return. Since generation takes 10-30 seconds, he implemented caching that prefills scenes and refills when stock drops below a threshold. Schomay demonstrates the game live, showing unique generated scenes including a pulsating blue light glade, a campfire scene, a dark cave, and foggy trees. He concludes with ideas for AI upscaling, contextual generation based on user location weather, and applying the process to other projects.

sections.title: Introduction and Game Concept
sections.summary: Jeff introduces his game where players wander a forest finding their way home before running out of courage, with encounters affecting Vigor and Courage stats. The original game had 16 scenes in a 4x4 grid, but he wanted to make every scene generated fresh for infinite exploration.

sections.title: Text Generation with OpenAI
sections.summary: Jeff describes scene definitions as JSON objects, starting with OpenAI's completion endpoint and detailed prompts. He then fine-tuned a model on 50 examples with simplified prompts, embedding format knowledge in training data. This cost about $1-2 total and produced perfect JSON output with fewer tokens.

sections.title: Image Generation with Leonardo
sections.summary: Jeff used Leonardo to create custom image models for stylistic consistency. The challenge was balancing consistent perspective, scale, forest setting, and tone with content variety (people, animals, buildings, empty scenes). He trained multiple models with different parameters before finding one that worked, producing cohesive yet unique images.

sections.title: Pipeline Assembly and Caching
sections.summary: Jeff built a simple asset server with an AI pipeline: request scene from OpenAI, validate JSON, send description to Leonardo for image, then assemble and return. Since generation takes 10-30 seconds, he implemented caching that prefills scenes and refills when stock drops below a threshold.

sections.title: Live Game Demo
sections.summary: Jeff demonstrates the game live, showing never-before-seen generated scenes including a pulsating blue light glade, a campfire scene, a dark cave, and foggy trees. He navigates the 4x4 grid, showing how courage depletion shrinks the viewport and vigor loss reduces speed.

sections.title: Closing Thoughts and Future Ideas
sections.summary: Jeff suggests adding an AI upscaler for higher resolution images (trading off time), enabling user-selected themes or contextual generation based on real-world weather/location, and applying the same process to other projects.
